title: Ackee and Saltfish
subtitle: Jamaica's national dish of ackee fruit with salted fish
excerpt: Ackee and saltfish is the national dish of Jamaica. Flaked salted fish is cooked with ackee -- the creamy, egg-like fruit of the ackee tree -- tomatoes, peppers, and thyme. It is eaten for breakfast and brunch throughout Jamaica. The ackee has a mild, buttery flavour that pairs perfectly with the salty fish.
sourceNotes: Ackee arrived in Jamaica from West Africa -- brought on slave ships from Ghana and Benin. The saltfish came from the colonial trade with Canada and New England, where cod was preserved in salt and shipped to the Caribbean. Together they became Jamaica's defining dish.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Soak the saltfish overnight. Everything else is quick to cook.

content.text: Tinned ackee is widely available in Caribbean grocery shops and most supermarkets. Drain it very carefully -- ackee is delicate and will break apart if handled roughly. Add it at the very end and fold it in gently rather than stirring.

items.prepNote: use salt cod or saltfish -- soak overnight to remove excess salt; or use smoked haddock as a substitute
use a 540g tin of ackee, drained

content.text: If using saltfish, soak it overnight in cold water, changing the water twice. If using smoked haddock, poach it in unsalted water for 8 minutes. Drain, flake the flesh, and discard the skin and bones.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and spring onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, peppers, and thyme. Cook for 4 minutes until the peppers soften.
Add the flaked fish. Stir gently to mix. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add the drained ackee. Fold in very gently so the pieces stay intact. Cook for 2 minutes until heated through.
Season with black pepper and chilli if using. Taste before adding any salt -- the fish may provide enough. Serve with fried dumplings, boiled green banana, or hard dough bread.

items.cause: Saltfish was not soaked long enough
items.fix: Always soak saltfish overnight with at least 2 water changes; taste the fish before adding and adjust the rest of the dish accordingly
Add ackee last and fold in very gently -- it breaks down quickly

items.cause: Some haddock is very strongly smoked
items.fix: Poach in plenty of unsalted water and change the water once during poaching to reduce the smokiness

content.text: Ackee and saltfish is the national dish of Jamaica. It is eaten for breakfast on Sundays across the island, served with fried dumplings, boiled green banana, and hard dough bread. The combination of West African ackee and North Atlantic preserved cod is a direct legacy of Jamaica's colonial history.
